question.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=7{x}^{3}+5x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $3\,\text{m}/\text{h}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=1\,\text{m}.$
question.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =7{x}^{3}+5x \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(7{x}^{3}+5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{x}^{3}+5x) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (21{x}^{2}+5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3\,\text{m}/\text{h}$ and $x=1$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =3\cdot (21\cdot {1}^{2}+5)\,\text{m}/\text{h} \\  & =78\,\text{m}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$
